Dear reader, let us first consider Einstein’s theory of special relativity. It postulates that time and space are interrelated - simply put, that the nearer one comes to *c*, or the speed of light, time dilates exponentially, to the point that at *c* time passes infinitely. Over the ages, people wondered, “What happens if someone goes *faster than light*?” They could not answer this, for they saw light speed as an impenetrable barrier none could cross. This, dear reader, is the tale of the man who flew faster than light. A tale of broken causality, beginnings, and most of all - the end of a universe.

#

Orocryx was content. His travels had yielded large amounts of time to improve his technology - decades had passed for him since the hail from the Voidborn, and it showed. He had installed an Alcubierre Drive in the engine bay, allowing him to push 1000*c*. Tachyon processor count was up 2048x, quantum encryption stonewalled snoopers, and the fusion reactor was replaced by an antimatter reactor and eventually a Blandford–Znajek Engine, pulling energy from dozens of black holes and producing on the order of 600 yottajoules a second. The fusion ramjet gave way to a directed matter drive, relativistic jets pushing even further, speed up to 15000*c* now. Let us consider, dear reader, **why** he was doing this. The simple fact is that once the lightspeed barrier is broken, time stops flowing and instead begins receding. Like a tide pulling the waves from a black sand beach, the flow of time recoils from those who dare to break the wall. Slowly at first, exponentially it would grow until years would tick past in a second. This was not enough for Orocryx, and that is why he went to the lengths he did. There were 10100 years or more to traverse.

#

Syra was godlike. From inside the Starjammer, she had access to devices that could vaporize galaxies in the blink of an eye, but even then Orocryx remained more powerful. Why? Orocryx, to make a long story short, had admin rights. Their target came up in their sensors, a proto-universe identified as one ripe for potential… *godly* life. Trivial scans indicated nothing but primal energy. *Good,* he thought, *this will be rich.* He parked the Starjammer in a distant corner of the universe, just outside of the bubble. Easily accessible, but so well hidden that none would notice it. With that, he decided to masquerade as one of the future gods - a name he needed, a name he would have, a name… *ah*. Tymoro. A good one, regal yet… interesting. An identity, for a more **primitive** universe. God of luck and chance? Acceptable. Calling up the nanoscale replicators, he made a cowl for the Eye, to make it seem like it simply wasn’t there. And so, he waited.

Many he met. XOM, Yuna, even Phyra. Many faded to nothingness - Ramen, Pome, Flox, the Trine Oligarchic Gods - but still many remained. All through the while he experimented with different things - such as the Gibberings, creatures that directly converted energy into mass, and the Deva, a race of rapidly technologically advancing humanoids, who some say he made them in his image. He saw the Images, monsters that copied all they saw, subject to the cube-square law in power increases. He saw the Sophons, a race that regarded basic electromagnetic principles and amplifiers as “magic”. They even made a railgun, how ***interesting***. All in all, it gave him time to think, time to work on his solution to the Voidborn problem. All the time in the universe he had - investigating the Primrose, the Deep, even peeking into the Nusquam, a pocket universe Oblitus though he had hidden well. Of all of them, Nztch Shamah intrigued him the most. An area where all elementary particles moved in tight synchronized circular orbits at 0.999999*c*, an effect that amounted to a slight vibration in everything, and a time dilation effect that sped up time for everything inside it and slowed it down to near-stillness for everything outside it. Syra recorded it all, and fed it into the databases for categorization, analysis, and eventual utilization at a later date. He saw the Sentinels, robots that captured everything and dropped it into Nztch Shamah - *Brute force, no use to me.* It was catalogued anyways. Yes, the universe was his sandbox, and he would play in it until he found a better way to brainstorm. Syra ran uncountable googols of calculations, finding better and better ways to cram thousands of carbon atoms in the densest possible configuration into the space of a single carbon atom, finding ways to stabilize denser and denser elements, investigating the lengths smaller and smaller particles could be pushed before snapping. Nothing interesting was gleaned except a few fun ideas, but it gave him more of the most valuable resource in existence: time.

The end of days came in a manner he had expected for too long. A telltale blot in the sky, kugelblitz trails streaming halfway across the sky… *Attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion…* Nothing mattered now, Gaea would burn in nuclear fire regardless. He wrapped up his projects as well as he could, then built his last construct in this doomed universe. A time bomb for a forgotten world, to keep it from Them. A trap in the finest way. Irony incarnate. He called the Starjammer to his position on the surface of Gaea, and vanished inside its bulk. A Deva, worn and weary from the floods, stumbled up to its invisible chassis and leaned upon it. “*Warp drive to 5%, let’s get out of here. Pulse jets… Fire.*” None noticed the bystander, caught in the Starjammer’s warp signature, thrown to the heavens, thrown to the universe Orocryx called home at its time of genesis. He was the first. The time bomb detonated, existence vanished, eaten by the supermassive black hole at the heart of the universe.

In their home universe they appeared, dragging with them the unwitting Deva. *”Accelerate to 0.9999999*c*, get us back within a day of when we left.*” “*Affirmative.”* The hyperdrive pulsed, and they were gone back at relativistic speeds, using time dilation to pass thousands of years in the blink of an eye. The lone Deva was left there, floating in the infinite dark.

Alone in the void of void, an unreality where nothing existed, not even nothing itself. Primal forces floated around him, and yet he was colder than cold itself.

*so cold…*
